newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's north braces for cyclone.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's north braces for cyclone.

text.p: The northeastern Australian state of Queensland braced on Tuesday for the arrival of tropical cyclone Justin, a massive storm system hovering menacingly off the Great Barrier Reef.

Hundreds of tourists were evacuated from the Whitsunday Islands and the biggest U.S.-Australian wargames since World War Two were put off for 24 hours as high winds and seas lashed the country's east coast.

Cyclone Justin, some 1,000 km (600 miles) wide and generating wind speeds at its core of up to 170 kph (105 mph), has been sitting in the Coral Sea about 620 kms (385 miles) off the tropical resort of Cairns.
But weather forecasters were unable to predict the level of destruction if, as expected, the cyclone moved over the coast in the next few days.
"We expect the cyclone to intensify a little today," said Jeffrey Crane, senior forecaster at the Australian Bureau of Meteorology.
"There has been almost no change overnight and no change in the cyclone's intensity," Crane told Reuters. "It depends on a southern ridge of high pressure which could cause the cyclone to move."

The cyclone was rated category two on a scale of five, although it could soon be upgraded to a category three. But Justin was not expected to reach the intensity of previous cyclones that have devastated coastal communities in Australia.
Although it is larger, experts said Justin lacked the "punch" of cyclone Tracy, which killed at least 65 people in 1974 when it ripped through the northern city of Darwin.
But the cyclone could still cause major crop damage. North Queensland is an important sugar cane growing area as well as being a major tourist draw because of the Great Barrier Reef.
The approaching storm has closed two bulk coal ports at Mackay and Hay Point.
Aircraft associated with the military exercise, Tandem Thrust 97, have been moved out of the area but commercial flights were operating normally.
